coverage.summary: General antitrust rule, not specific to housing. It applies to any person (as defined in § 16702, excluding end consumers) who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm, including landlords and rent-pricing vendors. It is not limited by building type, unit count, construction date or owner type.

evidence.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
“Person” has the same meaning as defined in Section 16702 and does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
Businesses in these industries should expect possible scrutiny under state law, but any business relying on a common pricing algorithm could be a target.

result.notes: Changes from the original coverage: (1) may_preempt_local_rules changed from false to null, because no document addresses the rule's relationship to local rules. (2) The summary's reference to local rent-algorithm bans in Berkeley, San Francisco, San Diego and Santa Ana was removed, because no captured document mentions them. (3) other_conditions set to null: the 'two or more persons' and 'competitor data' elements define the prohibited algorithm (conduct), not the covered buildings or owners. The single-firm/own-data carve-out from DX09 is likewise conduct-scope, so it belongs in exemptions or requirement rather than coverage. (4) requires_unknown_facts set to false: the rule applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm, not to a class of buildings that assessor data cannot identify. The rule has no building, unit-count or construction-date limits.
